| **2. CLI doctor** | _(pl"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"anned for v0.3.0)_ | — | — |

Web boot recovery (60 s budget)"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"Every 30 s the watchdog probes `http://127.0.0.1:$DSH_WEB_PORT/health`. After 3 consecutive failures"},{"id":"p10s2","text":" it enters the **triage** state machine, with a hard 60-second ceiling on total downtime per inciden"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"t enters the **triage** state machine, with a hard 60-second ceiling on total downtime per incident."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"**Simple path** (~10 s) — the most common case, a single broken plugin:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"1. Read the last 200 lines of the dsh web log.
2. Run **triage** against a regex pattern table (EADD"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"RINUSE, duplicate loader entry, schema parse error, module-not-found, plugin load error, …).
3. If t"},{"id":"p12s3","text":"he failing bundle is identified, **disable that single row** in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.ym"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"l` (write the change to a sibling `cordis.patch.yml.dr-disabled-<bundle>` file — your original is ne"},{"id":"p12s5","text":"ver edited).
4. Restart dsh web. The boot succeeds because the offending bundle is gone."},{"id":"p13s1","text":"**Complex path** (≤60 s) — multiple bundles, the simple path didn't work, or the failure is unknown:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"1. Drop a **safe-mode patch** into the profile that overrides every bundle with a no-op config (`saf"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"eMode: true`), except an explicit allow-list (`safeModeBundles`, default `["dsh-core"]`).
2. Restart"},{"id":"p14s3","text":" dsh web. The profile boots in safe mode — all your dsh_doctor_* tools are still available, every ot"},{"id":"p14s4","text":"her plugin is silenced.
3. Write a `restart-lock` marker so a `dsh doctor` invocation running in par"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"allel can skip the 60 s budget and work unbounded until safe mode is gone."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"**Invariants** enforced on every recovery:"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- The watchdog only kills the PID it reads from `~/.dsh/profiles/web/.dsh-web.pid`. It never invokes"},{"id":"p16s2","text":" `pkill`, `killall`, or any pattern-killer. The in-process doctor writes that file at apply() time w"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"ith process.pid (it runs inside dsh web, so that pid IS the web's); a stale pid reads as the already"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"-dead case the kill branch exists for.
- A sibling file pattern means your real `cordis.patch.yml` i"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"s never silently mutated. Inspect / revert at any time.
- If 60 s elapses without a healthy probe, t"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"he watchdog backs off and retries on the next probe tick instead of thrashing."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"### 2. Tool error capture"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"Every tool call in dsh passes through a `tools/*` cordis event waterfall. `dsh-doctor` subscribes to"},{"id":"p20s2","text":" `tools/execute` and `tools/post-execute` and runs every failed result through a **classifier** (def"},{"id":"p20s3","text":"ault: `transient` / `agent` / `business`) and a **policy** (default: record + log, optionally defer)"},{"id":"p20s4","text":".
